description: Browse the complete in-use keyword vocabulary or find existing words by meaning. Before setting keywords in add/update, use semantic mode with 1–20 concepts in queries and the target namespace (omit namespace when creating a new one); reuse candidates only when their meaning fits, otherwise new words are allowed. Similarity is not synonym equivalence. Metadata updates without keywords need no lookup. Literal mode matches one substring; browse takes no queries. Counts are scoped to live memories in namespace (omit for all). Semantic results include score and count, sorted by score; exact hits do not suppress related candidates. No search_id/report feedback is required. Pass the returned keyword_query_id to a later add/update/search when it informed your keyword choice. Unknown namespace returns namespace_not_found.

limit.description: Browse/literal default 50, max 100; semantic per-query default 5, max 20.

min_score.description: Semantic only, default 0.65. Lower to broaden candidates.

namespace.description: Optional live namespace; omitted means all.

offset.description: Pagination offset; must be 0 in semantic mode.

queries.description: One nonblank string for literal, 1–20 for semantic; omit for browse.

sort_by.description: Browse/literal: count (default) or keyword. Semantic: score only.

name: list_keywords

description: Store a new memory. Text is automatically embedded for semantic search. You MUST provide a concise, faithful summary in the summary parameter; keep technical terms, ticket numbers, and business event times. The server still accepts a missing or blank summary and stores a deterministic extract from the leading sentence or line as a reliability fallback. Deduplicated by content+namespace: if the same text already exists in the target namespace, no duplicate is inserted and the existing record's id is returned with created=false. Before adding, call 'list_keywords' in semantic mode with your keyword concepts and target namespace; for a new namespace, omit the namespace during lookup. Call 'stats' for category_counts. Reuse an existing keyword/category when semantically appropriate; create a new one only when no existing value matches. Pass keywords as an array in metadata.keywords — they are content concepts (e.g. entities, topics). For each new memory, provide 1–3 relevant categories in metadata.categories to describe its nature/classification; prefer these canonical categories: requirement, business-rule, design, data-model, api, pattern, convention, bugfix, performance, refactor, migration, verification, research, investigation, incident, config, tooling, ops, glossary, other. When adding a memory or changing its text, provide metadata.anchors: 0-5 distinctive identifiers present in the content that a future query could use to identify it (names, classes, APIs, error codes, config keys, versions). Keywords describe topics; anchors identify specific things. Select anchors from the content, preserve their spelling, and do not invent them or copy generic keywords. Pass [] when there are none. Explicit anchors replace the old list; [] clears it. Changing text without resubmitting anchors clears old anchors; metadata-only and whitespace-equivalent text updates preserve them when omitted. An unknown namespace is rejected without writing; call 'stats' to see the available namespaces, then retry with confirm_codes=["namespace_not_found"] to deliberately create a new one.

confirm_codes.description: Confirmation codes for validation rules you deliberately override. Pass ["namespace_not_found"] to create a namespace that does not exist yet. Unknown codes are ignored; format/length/reserved-word checks cannot be bypassed.

keyword_query_id.description: Optional ID from list_keywords when its candidates informed this write; audit linkage only.

anchors.description: When adding a memory or changing its text, provide metadata.anchors: 0-5 distinctive identifiers present in the content that a future query could use to identify it (names, classes, APIs, error codes, config keys, versions). Keywords describe topics; anchors identify specific things. Select anchors from the content, preserve their spelling, and do not invent them or copy generic keywords. Pass [] when there are none. Explicit anchors replace the old list; [] clears it. Changing text without resubmitting anchors clears old anchors; metadata-only and whitespace-equivalent text updates preserve them when omitted. Each anchor must be non-empty and at most 128 characters after NFKC and whitespace normalization; invalid input is rejected.

categories.description: For a new memory provide 1-3 relevant categories describing its nature/classification. Prefer canonical values; introduce a new one only when none fits: requirement, business-rule, design, data-model, api, pattern, convention, bugfix, performance, refactor, migration, verification, research, investigation, incident, config, tooling, ops, glossary, other. Normalized to lowercase.

keywords.description: Content keywords (concrete concepts in the memory, not category/type). Prefer reusing existing keywords from list_keywords semantic candidates; create a new keyword only when none fits. Normalized to lowercase.

namespace.description: Namespace (default: $MEMORY_DEFAULT_NAMESPACE or 'default'). The configured default namespace is always valid; other namespaces must already exist unless confirm_codes includes 'namespace_not_found'.

summary.description: A concise summary of text. LLM callers MUST provide this; missing or blank values are tolerated and replaced with a deterministic leading-text extract.

text.description: The memory text. Keep long project documents in the repository and store only a concise summary and file path here; oversized input is rejected rather than silently truncated.

name: add

description: Semantic search across memories by query text. Use this for topic/keyword questions — e.g. "what do we know about X", "anything related to Y" — where you want the most semantically similar memories. Results return the memory summary (falling back to a deterministic leading-text extract when absent); call 'get_details' with the returned IDs to fetch full content. For time-based questions (e.g. "what did we do recently / last session") use 'search_meta' with sort_by='updated_at' instead. When you know the memory's keyword or category, pass keywords= and/or categories= to pre-filter candidates before similarity scoring. Exact index values are used directly; unmatched values are semantically resolved to the closest existing values in the same dimension and namespace. For exploratory questions, omit filters to keep the full candidate set. Use 'list_keywords' or 'stats' to inspect existing values. The response reports the applied mapping in filter_resolution. Values within each dimension use OR; keywords and categories combine with each other and namespace using AND. If no results are found, inspect filter_resolution when filters were supplied, or call 'stats' to verify the namespace before retrying. If the response has response_code='namespace_not_found', the requested namespace does not exist; use response_meta.known_namespaces or omit the namespace to search all namespaces.

categories.description: Use when the desired memory nature/classification is known. Restrict candidates to memories carrying any of these categories (OR) before memory-text cosine scoring. Exact values win; unmatched words are semantically resolved within the same namespace. Omit for broad discovery. Combined with keywords and namespace using AND.

k.description: Max number of results to return (default: 5). Increase this (e.g. 20) when searching broadly or if results seem sparse.

keyword_query_id.description: Optional ID from list_keywords; audit linkage only.

keywords.description: Use when the desired content concept is known. Restrict candidates to memories carrying any of these keywords (OR) before memory-text cosine scoring. Exact values win; unmatched words are semantically resolved within the same namespace. Omit for broad discovery. Combined with categories and namespace using AND.

namespace.description: Only search within this namespace (optional). Leave empty to search all namespaces. An unknown namespace returns response_code='namespace_not_found' with the available list instead of an empty success; call 'stats' to see available namespaces.

query.description: Search text — automatically embedded for semantic similarity matching

threshold.description: Minimum similarity score 0-1 (default: 0 = no filter). Higher values return fewer but more relevant results. Keep at 0 unless you want to narrow down.

name: search_semantic

description: Exact-term (lexical) search over memory text using full-text matching (SQLite FTS5 / BM25). Use this for literal identifiers, error codes, class or symbol names, version numbers and distinctive phrases that semantic search may miss — e.g. "PoolAcquirePendingLimitException", "ORA-00060", "subscriptionsPerConnection". It matches memory CONTENT only (not keywords/categories) and requires an actual term match, so it does not generalise to paraphrases; use 'search_semantic' for topic or conceptual questions. Continuous Chinese text is not segmented in this index, so use 'search_semantic' for Chinese queries rather than 'search_lexical'. Results return the memory summary; call 'get_details' with the returned IDs for full content. Scores are BM25-based and are NOT comparable with search_semantic scores. If no results are found, call 'stats' to verify the namespace, or retry with 'search_semantic'. If the response has response_code='namespace_not_found', the requested namespace does not exist; use response_meta.known_namespaces or omit the namespace to search all namespaces.

k.description: Max number of results to return (default: 10, range 1-100).

namespace.description: Only search within this namespace (optional). Leave empty to search all namespaces. An unknown namespace returns response_code='namespace_not_found'.

query.description: Literal text or terms to match. The query's terms are OR-combined; long identifiers may be split on punctuation, so include the distinctive parts.

name: search_lexical

description: Search the retrieval anchors a memory declared — distinctive identifiers, names, class/API names, error codes, config keys, versions. Use this when the query contains distinctive terms likely to appear in a declared anchor (e.g. a class name or ticket id). It matches the ANCHORS field only (not memory text, keywords or categories), so it can be narrower than 'search_lexical' and 'search_semantic'; retry with those when it returns nothing. Results return the memory summary; call 'get_details' with the returned IDs for full content. Scores are BM25-based and are NOT comparable with the other search scores. If the response has response_code='namespace_not_found', the requested namespace does not exist; use response_meta.known_namespaces or omit the namespace to search all namespaces.

k.description: Max number of results to return (default: 10, range 1-100).

namespace.description: Only search within this namespace (optional). Leave empty to search all namespaces. An unknown namespace returns response_code='namespace_not_found'.

query.description: Anchor text to match. The query's terms are OR-combined.

name: search_anchor

description: List memories by exact criteria: keywords, categories, namespace, updated_at time range, sort order and pagination. Results return the memory summary (falling back to a deterministic leading-text extract when absent); call 'get_details' with the returned IDs to fetch full content. Use this for time-based questions such as "what did we do recently / last session" — combine sort_by='updated_at' with a small limit to get the most recently written or changed memories. For fuzzy/topic/keyword questions use 'search_semantic' instead. For keyword filtering, call 'list_keywords'; use 'stats' for categories in category_counts. Multiple keywords match ANY (OR), and multiple categories match ANY (OR). Keywords/categories combine with namespace and time filters using AND. For relative time windows ("last week", "this month"), call 'stats' first to get server_time, then pass concrete updated_after/updated_before timestamps. Ordered by the given field descending (default: created_at). If the response has response_code='namespace_not_found', the requested namespace does not exist; use response_meta.known_namespaces or omit the namespace to list all memories.

categories.description: Filter by memory categories — any match is sufficient (OR). Call 'stats' first to see canonical categories in category_counts.

keyword_query_id.description: Optional ID from list_keywords; audit linkage only.

keywords.description: Filter by global keywords — any match is sufficient (OR). Call 'list_keywords' to find available keywords.

limit.description: Max results (default: 100). Use a small value (e.g. 5-10) for recent-memory lookups.

namespace.description: Only list memories in this namespace (optional). Leave empty to list all namespaces. An unknown namespace returns response_code='namespace_not_found' with the available list instead of an empty success.

sort_by.description: Sort field, descending. Default: created_at. Use 'updated_at' for most recently written/changed first.

updated_after.description: ISO8601 timestamp (e.g. '2026-07-01T00:00:00+00:00'). Only return memories updated after this moment (exclusive). If the user asks for a relative window (e.g. 'last week', 'this month') and you are unsure of the current date, call 'stats' first to get its 'server_time', then compute this value.

updated_before.description: ISO8601 timestamp (e.g. '2026-07-01T00:00:00+00:00'). Only return memories updated before this moment (exclusive). If the user asks for a relative window (e.g. 'last week', 'this month') and you are unsure of the current date, call 'stats' first to get its 'server_time', then compute this value.

name: search_meta

description: Fetch full content for one or more memories by ID. Pass an array of IDs, including for a single memory. Returns the complete text of each found memory plus the list of IDs that do not exist (partial success). Use this when a search result summary looks relevant and you need the full original content.

memory_ids.description: Array of memory IDs to fetch full content for; use a one-element array for a single ID.

source_search_id.description: Optional search_id from the search whose results prompted this lookup; audit linkage only.

name: get_details

description: Update a memory's text, summary, metadata and/or namespace. When changing text, you MUST also provide a concise, faithful summary for the new text. The server still accepts an omitted or blank summary and stores a deterministic leading-text extract as a reliability fallback. A summary may also be corrected without changing text; metadata-only updates leave it untouched. Long project documents belong in the repository; store only their concise summary and path in memory. Oversized text is rejected, never silently truncated. When changing the memory text, provide 1–3 relevant categories in metadata.categories for the updated memory; metadata-only changes can preserve existing categories. When updating metadata you may pass metadata.keywords — content concepts; reuse existing keywords from list_keywords semantic candidates when one fits; an empty array clears. You may also pass metadata.categories — memory nature/classification, up to 3 values, prefer the canonical categories from stats' category_counts: requirement, business-rule, design, data-model, api, pattern, convention, bugfix, performance, refactor, migration, verification, research, investigation, incident, config, tooling, ops, glossary, other. An empty array clears the memory's categories. When adding a memory or changing its text, provide metadata.anchors: 0-5 distinctive identifiers present in the content that a future query could use to identify it (names, classes, APIs, error codes, config keys, versions). Keywords describe topics; anchors identify specific things. Select anchors from the content, preserve their spelling, and do not invent them or copy generic keywords. Pass [] when there are none. Explicit anchors replace the old list; [] clears it. Changing text without resubmitting anchors clears old anchors; metadata-only and whitespace-equivalent text updates preserve them when omitted. Moving a memory to an unknown namespace is rejected; call 'stats' to see the available namespaces, then retry with confirm_codes=["namespace_not_found"] to deliberately create a new one.

confirm_codes.description: Confirmation codes for validation rules you deliberately override. Pass ["namespace_not_found"] to move the memory into a namespace that does not exist yet. Unknown codes are ignored; format/length/reserved-word checks cannot be bypassed.

keyword_query_id.description: Optional ID from list_keywords when its candidates informed this update; audit linkage only.

anchors.description: When adding a memory or changing its text, provide metadata.anchors: 0-5 distinctive identifiers present in the content that a future query could use to identify it (names, classes, APIs, error codes, config keys, versions). Keywords describe topics; anchors identify specific things. Select anchors from the content, preserve their spelling, and do not invent them or copy generic keywords. Pass [] when there are none. Explicit anchors replace the old list; [] clears it. Changing text without resubmitting anchors clears old anchors; metadata-only and whitespace-equivalent text updates preserve them when omitted. Each anchor must be non-empty and at most 128 characters after NFKC and whitespace normalization; invalid input is rejected.

categories.description: When changing text, provide 1-3 relevant categories describing the updated memory's nature/classification. Prefer canonical values; introduce a new one only when none fits: requirement, business-rule, design, data-model, api, pattern, convention, bugfix, performance, refactor, migration, verification, research, investigation, incident, config, tooling, ops, glossary, other. Metadata-only updates may omit this field; empty array clears.

keywords.description: Content keywords (concrete concepts in the memory, not category/type). Prefer reusing existing keywords from list_keywords semantic candidates; create a new keyword only when none fits. Normalized to lowercase. Empty array clears.

namespace.description: New namespace. The configured default namespace is always valid; other namespaces must already exist unless confirm_codes includes 'namespace_not_found'. Blank/omitted leaves it unchanged.

source_search_id.description: Optional search_id that prompted this update; audit linkage only.

summary.description: New summary. LLM callers changing text MUST provide this; omission is tolerated and uses a deterministic leading-text extract.

text.description: New text. Oversized content is rejected; keep long documents in the repository and save a summary/path here.

name: update

description: Soft-delete a memory by ID. It is removed from all search results.
name: delete

description: Storage statistics. Returns 'total' (record count), 'namespace_counts' (map of namespace -> record count, e.g. check namespaces before search/add to avoid missing results or creating duplicates), 'keyword_total' (the global number of distinct in-use keywords; use list_keywords to browse or find words), 'category_counts' (seed categories, always listed with count 0 when unused, plus any custom categories in use; prefer seed values, up to 3 per memory), and 'server_time' (current UTC time). Check 'server_time' first when a user asks a time-based question (e.g. "what did we do last week / this month") so you can compute the correct updated_after/updated_before values for the 'search_meta' tool. The default namespace is set via MEMORY_DEFAULT_NAMESPACE env var.
name: stats

description: Report how helpful a previous search's results were for the current question or context. After using results from search_semantic, search_lexical, search_anchor or search_meta, pass its search_id plus ratings per memory id. Only IDs returned by that nonempty search are accepted. rating must be an integer from -10 to 10: positive = helpful (larger = more useful), negative = misleading/interference (more negative = stronger interference), 0 = neither helpful nor harmful. You may rate any nonempty subset of the returned ids. Declare feedback_source and feedback_purpose so audit can separate task feedback from tests; these are caller declarations, not verified human identity. Reports from an earlier server process or expired searches are rejected.

feedback_purpose.description: Optional caller-declared use: task, evaluation, or test. Omitted means unspecified.

feedback_source.description: Optional caller-declared origin: llm, human, or test. Omitted means unspecified; this does not verify human identity.

ratings.description: Rate 1–1000 distinct IDs returned by this search. Values outside -10..10 or non-integers are rejected.

m_id.description: Memory id from the search results

search_id.description: The search_id from a recent nonempty search_semantic/search_lexical/search_anchor/search_meta response in this server process

name: report
